clue.text: Rise and lambaste church? It's just fate

parts.note: to rise is to come up
to lambaste is to pan, criticise harshly
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone who stands up and attacks the church is told whatever befalls them is deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting what you deserve is a just fate, the idiomatic sense of a fitting punishment.

clue.text: Gigantic bird biting head off dangerous reptile

indicators.note: the reptile's name loses its first letter, as if its head were bitten away

parts.note: a croc, short for crocodile, is a dangerous reptile

explanation.surface: A huge bird attacks a crocodile and bites its head off.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is the enormous mythical bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad's voyages.

clue.text: Silk suit's outside in ditch perhaps

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the obstacle word

parts.note: a ditch is one kind of barrier

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word suit, its first and last, are taken

explanation.surface: A silk suit's outer layer ends up in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silk' is a Queen's (now King's) Counsel, a senior British barrister, so called from the silk gown. ST, the outside of 'suit', goes 'in' BARRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: In British legal slang a silk is a senior courtroom lawyer who has taken silk as a KC or QC.

clue.text: Requirement of string players over in Toscanini's orchestra

indicators.note: over says the run of letters is read in the other direction
the letters sit inside the words Toscanini's orchestra

explanation.surface: Something the string section needs, in the great conductor's orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks NISOR from tosca(NINI'S OR)chestra; 'over' turns it round. Toscanini was a famous Italian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists and cellists rub this resin on their bows so the hair grips the strings.

clue.text: Ring round, engaging half of boys for game

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them

indicators.note: the first half of the word boys is taken

parts.note: O is round, the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A ring goes round a group of boys playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a noun but is the verb, to phone; 'engaging' signals the insertion of half the boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a spool is spun and tossed on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: In French port, perhaps, without time to knit

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the pieces surround the letter

parts.note: en is French for in
port is an example of a wine

explanation.surface: Someone in a French port, with no time, tries to knit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour; it is the fortified wine. 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit things together is to interlace or twist them into one, a close synonym.

clue.text: Stand-in senior officer backed with little hesitation

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, a senior officer
um is the small noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A deputy is supported by a senior officer with only a slight pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like supported; here it signals a reversal of the colonel's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily covers for another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Disinclined to engineer rental cut

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or arrange, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to arrange a reduction in rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant means being unwilling or disinclined to do something.

clue.text: Rulers using terminus move in rain regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Rulers order the train terminus to be moved in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'terminus move in rain' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a triumvir was one of three men sharing power, so a group of such men were rulers.

clue.text: Person like Brezhnev gripped by firm statement of belief

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
Brezhnev was a Soviet leader, so a communist, a Red

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader held firmly to his statement of belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a formal declaration of what one believes, from Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Declined to unite during ball, perhaps

indicators.note: during means placed in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a red is a ball, for example in snooker or a red cricket ball
to fuse things is to unite them

explanation.surface: Someone said no to joining up at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance; it is a snooker red, one of the red balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To have refused is to have declined, both meaning turned down.

clue.text: Adjusting to 23 he aims to get a bull

definitions.text: he aims to get a bull

indicators.note: adjusting means altering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the number refers to the solution of 23 down, a play or stage work

explanation.surface: A man adapts himself to a play, aiming to win a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he aims to get a bull' sounds like darts, but it means someone who sets out to kill a bull in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter's goal in the ring is to kill the bull, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Hoofed mammal, one following pensioner round end of park

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the rest
round means around, so the pensioner encloses the next letter

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word park

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hoofed animal follows an old pensioner around the edge of the park.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) goes 'round' K, the 'end of' park; I comes after it, 'following'.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a hoofed African mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: In the north, force deployed after breaching part of defence

indicators.note: breaching means breaking into the wall, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a wall is part of a defensive fortification

indicators.note: deployed means spread out into position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In the north, troops are deployed to breach part of the defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' is a northern English dialect word for a waterfall, from Old Norse; 'deployed' scrambles 'after' and 'breaching' sets it inside the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England, from Old Norse foss, a force is a cascade such as Aira Force.

clue.text: Star identified by seamen once going west

indicators.note: going west in an across clue means reading right to left

parts.note: the NUS was the National Union of Seamen, now merged

explanation.surface: A star is spotted by old-time sailors heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Seamen was a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Our sun is a star, the nearest one to Earth.

clue.text: Stuck for somewhere to put patient, move on quickly

parts.note: stuck fast means firmly stuck
a hospital ward is where a patient is put

explanation.surface: With nowhere to put a patient, the doctor skips ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast-forward is to skip ahead, as on a recording, so to move on quickly.

clue.text: Source of bread for male swan

definitions.meaning: a round loaf, or the corn ear that gives flour
the term for a male swan, the female being a pen

explanation.definitionFit: A cob is both a rounded loaf of bread and the name for a male swan.

clue.text: Woman a Gershwin musical initially upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word musical

explanation.surface: A woman is upset by a Gershwin musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole run A + IRA + M round.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a woman's name, as in West Side Story or The Sound of Music.

clue.text: I'm bent on higher education, ditching last of the school garb, perhaps?

parts.note: uni, short for university, is higher education

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the letter is removed

parts.note: if I'm bent on something, it is for me

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A student keen on going to university sheds the last of their school clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm bent on higher education' reads as UNI FOR ME; 'ditching' removes E, the 'last of' 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A school uniform is an example of the garb pupils wear, hence the perhaps.

clue.text: Perfume: possible prize for French and Scripture

parts.note: a pot is slang for a trophy cup
pour is French for for
RI is religious instruction, the old British school subject

explanation.surface: A scented prize is awarded for French and Scripture lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices used to scent a room.

clue.text: Move slowly without resistance, like the Valkyries?

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, enclosing the letter

parts.note: to nose forward is to move slowly and carefully
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Creeping along unopposed, like the warrior maidens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Valkyries come from Old Norse mythology, so they are Norse.

clue.text: Inconstant criteria I must leave for revision

indicators.note: the named letter has to go from the word criteria
revision means reworking, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unreliable criteria must be dropped for review.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one I out of CRITERIA ('must leave') and rearrange the rest ('for revision').
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic is irregular and unpredictable, hence inconstant.

clue.text: Send down girl who's out of practice, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are said aloud

parts.note: a girl named Kate who is rusty, out of practice

explanation.surface: Expel the girl whose skills have slipped, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' is British university slang for expel; to rusticate is to suspend a student for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, rustication is suspension from college, a form of being sent down.

clue.text: Music-lover in court, formerly right energetic type!

indicators.note: in means placed inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: once means formerly
a goer is an energetic, lively person

explanation.surface: A music fan appears in court, once a lively sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends performances regularly is a music-lover.

clue.text: Cut out port our transatlantic allies finding harmful

parts.note: to delete is to cut out
Rio de Janeiro is a port
the US, the British setter's allies across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A port is cut out of trade, and the Americans find that damaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleterious means causing harm or damage, a formal synonym.

clue.text: If he can't, I could become clan leader

indicators.note: could become means the letters may change into a new order

explanation.surface: One clansman says that if the leader fails, he will take over.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a Scottish clan or tribe.

clue.text: Recurring theme Tom set up in undemanding-sounding poem

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other pieces
sounding says the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: light reading or work is undemanding
If is Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom is placed in an easy-sounding poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses Tom, which goes 'in' between the homophone of light ('undemanding') and Kipling's poem; the hyphenated 'undemanding-sounding' hides the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring musical or literary theme tied to a character or idea.

clue.text: Old woman's argument for getting large dog

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old woman, plus the possessive s
a tiff is a minor argument

explanation.surface: A mother's quarrel over getting a big dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a very large, powerful breed of dog.

clue.text: One supplying needs of three queens, perhaps?

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen
a second ER, another queen

explanation.surface: Who caters for three queens at once?
explanation.walkthrough: A queen can be a female cat as well as ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink, meeting the needs of guests.

clue.text: Teachers describing western uplands

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the letters enclose the next one

parts.note: dons are university teachers

explanation.surface: Teachers describe the hills of the west.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Downs are rolling chalk uplands, such as the South Downs.

clue.text: Medical practitioner with a degree in theatre studies?

parts.note: Dr is a doctor
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A doctor holding a degree in theatre studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre studies is the academic subject of plays and performance.

clue.text: Came first, being sort of light

definitions.meaning: went in front, headed the field

explanation.definitionFit: Led is the past tense of lead, to come first, and an LED is a light-emitting diode.
